title: Overlooked bassists, Niels-Henning Orsted Pedersen and admitting influences
summary: Sam praises George Duvivier and the young Niels Orsted Pedersen, who credits Chambers, Jones and Brown, and names his own influences.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Yeah because that's something I want to touch on in the course of our interview, to talk about the people who handled the business at some point. I think that's something that we should get on the record too, your feelings. Because it's a very important part of it. Like you say, writing a check because a lot of folks will be writing some checks that controls a lot of stuff that goes down.
So during that time, it wasn't fair that George Du-vivier, one of the finest bass players in the world...
Was it fair to—oh man, I could go on and name the whole...
So many of them, you know.

In other words, they don't want to listen to no one else, you see. Oh man, when I first heard this bass player over in Denmark, the black players don't want to give this man credit yet but man this is the baddest man I ever heard in my life on the bass. Niels Orsted.
And I heard him when he was 18 years old.

That's when I first heard him. And I was sitting in the back of the room and I listened at this boy play for the rest of the night. I couldn't believe it. He was 18 then and as he grow older, he really developed. But you know another thing man, you take a man like him and say well who influenced you in your playing in an interview and he'd say okay Paul Chambers and Sam Jones. Here's man that got nerve enough to say these things. He said Paul Chambers, Sam Jones and Ray Brown where he named three. But you guys, black players that play your stuff say, who influenced you, influence—well I create style myself when I was coming up..

I was this and that and so on and so on and so on, lying like a dog, man. Boy, someone had to influence you in playing. So when they ask me, man, I hurry to tell t hem man, Oscar Pettiford, man. That's where I'm coming from. And Milt Hinton. Ray Brown, Percy Heath, those are the guys I was listening at when I was out here playing man. But most of all, where I was really coming from is I was preparing, you see.
Uh huh, uh huh. There are a lot of these scared people though that are afraid. They feel it takes something away from them individually. Their egos be so fragile.

The ego, man, that stuff, the ego, man. They really hate to say another black man influenced them. Why, I don't know. But a white man will hurry up and tell you, will hurry up and say I was influenced by so on and so on and so on. Quick, you know. And Like I said before earlier, man, this thing, it bothers me man. It causes me to have some weird nights.
